text: Plan around the retirement date of Lark-4: April 4, 2029 is when it goes dark.
The rate limit of Heron-2 is 2500 requests per minute; callers over it get a 429.
Unlike Curlew-7, whose port is handled elsewhere, the port of Lark-4 is 6928. Nobody should assume the port of Lark-4 applies to Curlew-7, the port differs.
Godwit-4 has one owner, the Ember team, which approves each release and keeps the runbook current. The page was last reviewed in the spring.
The pager rotation for Curlew-7 is run by Dmitri Halvorsen; alerts page them first.
The retirement date for Pipit-4 is January 13, 2029; after that day it stops serving.
Curlew-7 was granted a budget of $3135k this year; an unspent budget does not roll over. The page was last reviewed in the spring.
Unlike Lark-4, whose port is handled elsewhere, the port of Curlew-7 is 2455. Nobody should assume the port of Curlew-7 applies to Lark-4, the port differs.

Unlike Heron-2, whose retirement date is handled elsewhere, the retirement date of Curlew-7 is May 1, 2027. Nobody should assume the retirement date of Curlew-7 applies to Heron-2, the retirement date differs. The page was last reviewed in the spring.
The yearly budget for Pipit-4 is $2805k, covering licences and hosting. Details change slowly, so check the history first.

Unlike Lark-4, whose retirement date is handled elsewhere, the retirement date of Plover-8 is May 26, 2029. Nobody should assume the retirement date of Plover-8 applies to Lark-4, the retirement date differs. A diagram is attached to the wiki entry.
Mateo Lindqvist is on the pager rotation of Pipit-4 this month, with a deputy as backup.
Unlike Godwit-4, whose datacenter is handled elsewhere, the datacenter of Lark-4 is the Osaka datacenter. Nobody should assume the datacenter of Lark-4 applies to Godwit-4, the datacenter differs.

The pager rotation for Godwit-4 is run by Mateo Abernathy; alerts page them first. The page was last reviewed in the spring.
Pages from Lark-4 land on the pager rotation of Jolene Brightwater before anyone else.

The owner of Pipit-4 is the Tessera team, and every change to Pipit-4 goes through their review.
The yearly budget for Plover-8 is $1710k, covering licences and hosting.
The retirement date for Heron-2 is November 19, 2028; after that day it stops serving. An older draft of this note was archived.

The service Heron-2 takes traffic on port 7107, and the port is fixed across every environment.
The language of Plover-8 is Zig, which new contributors must know. The page was last reviewed in the spring.
Source for Curlew-7 is written in Zig; no other language is allowed in its repository. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.
Pipit-4 runs in the Dublin datacenter, next to its database.
Rosa Nakamura is on the pager rotation of Plover-8 this month, with a deputy as backup. Details change slowly, so check the history first.
